title: Spinal Cord Injury: Deeper Assessment and Neurogenic Shock
next: Chapter 25, Lesson 2: Spinal motion restriction, head-injury targets, and complications

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already hold the head, apply a collar and package the patient. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Link the anatomy to what you see: breathing, shock, weakness
  2. Tell spinal shock, neurogenic shock and bleeding apart
  3. Do a baseline neuro exam and know what BC asks of a PCP

Textbook: Chapter 25, PDF pages 2093–2132
slides.say: Welcome to class. As EMRs, you already know spinal care well: you hold the head, apply a hard collar, and package the patient. In BC, the Spinal Management protocol is the same for every licence level, so the hands-on steps don't change. What changes is the thinking. As a PCP, you're expected to explain what the injury is doing to breathing and circulation, to recognize neurogenic shock, and to record a neurological baseline the hospital can compare against. Today we'll cover the anatomy that matters, the kinds of shock after a spinal injury, and a PCP-level assessment.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。作为 EMR，你们对脊柱处置已经很熟：扶住头部、上硬颈托、固定好病人。在 BC，脊柱管理流程对所有执照级别都一样，所以动手的步骤不变，变的是思考。作为 PCP，你要能解释损伤对呼吸和循环做了什么，识别神经源性休克，并记录一份医院可以对比的神经系统基线。今天讲：要紧的解剖、脊柱损伤后的几种“休克”，以及 PCP 水平的评估。

slides.title: The cord levels that matter
slides.body:
LevelWhy it matters on scene
C3–C5Phrenic nerve → diaphragm; injury can stop breathing
Low neck to T2Rib muscles lost; belly breathing, weak cough
T6 and aboveSympathetic outflow cut → neurogenic shock
L2Cord ends; cauda equina below

The vagus nerve doesn't run through the cord, so it keeps slowing the heart after the injury.
slides.say: Let's start with the levels that change what you see on scene. A handy phrase: C three, four and five keep the diaphragm alive. The phrenic nerve, which drives the diaphragm, leaves the cord at C3 to C5, so an injury at or above that level can stop breathing. An injury lower in the neck, down to about T2, can paralyse the rib muscles, leaving the diaphragm to work alone. At T6 and above, an injury can cut the sympathetic nerves, the body's fight-or-flight system. The cord ends at about L2. And the vagus nerve, which slows the heart, doesn't run through the cord, so it keeps working.
slides.sayZh: 先看会改变现场表现的节段。记住一句：“C3、4、5 保膈肌”。驱动膈肌的膈神经从 C3 到 C5 发出，所以这个平面或更高的损伤可能让呼吸停止。颈下段、大约到 T2 的损伤可以让肋间肌瘫痪，只剩膈肌在工作。T6 及以上的损伤可能切断交感神经，也就是身体的“战斗或逃跑”系统。脊髓大约在 L2 结束。而负责减慢心跳的迷走神经不经过脊髓，所以照样工作。

slides.title: Primary and secondary injury
slides.body:
Primary: the impact→Secondary: swelling, inflammation→More cord lost
  • Primary damage happens in a moment: you can't undo it
  • Secondary damage grows over the following hours
  • Made worse by low oxygen, low blood sugar, cold
  • Your care: neutral line, less motion, oxygen, perfusion, warmth
slides.say: Every spinal cord injury has two parts. The primary injury happens at the moment of impact: a bone fragment, a stretch, a bullet. You can't undo it. The secondary injury comes afterwards, as swelling and inflammation spread, and it gets worse when the cord is short of oxygen, short of sugar, or cold. Think of a small kitchen fire: the first flame is the primary injury, but how much of the house burns depends on what happens next. Motion restriction and neutral alignment protect the cord mechanically; oxygen, perfusion, warmth and a normal blood sugar protect it chemically. As a PCP, you have more tools for perfusion.
slides.sayZh: 每一处脊髓损伤都分两部分。原发性损伤发生在撞击瞬间：一块骨片、一次牵拉、一颗子弹，无法逆转。继发性损伤随后到来，肿胀和炎症向外扩散，脊髓缺氧、缺糖或受冷时会更严重。想象厨房里的小火：第一团火苗是原发性损伤，但整栋房子烧掉多少，取决于接下来发生什么。脊柱活动限制和中立位在机械上保护脊髓；氧气、灌注、保暖和正常血糖在化学上保护它。作为 PCP，你在灌注方面有了更多工具。

slides.title: Cord syndromes: know the patterns
slides.body:
Complete: all function lost below the level. Incomplete: some spared, so recovery is possible.

SyndromeTypical causeWhat you find
Anterior cordFlexion, bone fragmentsParalysis; pain, temperature, touch lost
Central cordOlder neck forced backwardArms weaker than legs
Brown-SéquardPenetrating: half the cord cutSame side weak; other side loses pain, temperature
slides.say: Cord injuries are complete or incomplete. Complete means all function below the injury is lost. Incomplete means some is spared, so the patient can still recover, which is why careful handling matters. Anterior cord syndrome usually follows flexion or bone fragments: paralysis, and loss of pain, temperature and touch below the injury. Central cord syndrome is typical in an older person whose neck is forced backward, for example falling forward onto the face: the arms are weaker than the legs. Brown-Séquard syndrome is half the cord cut, often by a knife: weakness and lost position sense on the injured side, lost pain and temperature on the other side.
slides.sayZh: 脊髓损伤分完全性和不完全性。完全性指损伤以下功能全部丧失；不完全性指保留了一部分，病人仍可能恢复，这正是小心搬动的意义。前索综合征多见于屈曲伤或骨片压迫：瘫痪，损伤以下痛觉、温度觉和触觉丧失。中央索综合征典型见于颈部被迫后仰的老人，比如向前摔倒、面部着地：上肢比下肢更无力。Brown-Séquard 综合征是脊髓被切断一半，常见于刀伤：受伤一侧无力、位置觉丧失，对侧痛温觉丧失。

slides.q: A 79-year-old trips and falls forward, striking her forehead on the floor. She can stand, but both hands are weak and burning. Which pattern fits best?
slides.say: Let's check. A seventy-nine-year-old trips and falls forward, striking her forehead on the floor. She can stand, but both hands are weak and burning. Which pattern fits best? A, anterior cord syndrome. B, central cord syndrome. C, Brown-Séquard syndrome. D, posterior cord syndrome. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检查一下。一位七十九岁的老人绊倒向前摔，额头撞到地板。她能站起来，但双手无力、有烧灼感。哪种模式最符合？A 前索综合征；B 中央索综合征；C Brown-Séquard 综合征；D 后索综合征。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, central cord syndrome. A fall onto the forehead forces an older neck backward and squeezes the centre of the cord, so the arms suffer more than the legs. Anterior cord syndrome paralyses everything below the injury, legs included. Brown-Séquard affects the two sides differently, usually after a stab wound. Posterior cord syndrome removes light touch and position sense but keeps strength. And although she can stand, her new neuro signs mean she still needs motion restriction.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，中央索综合征。额头着地会迫使老年人的颈部后仰，挤压脊髓中央部，所以上肢比下肢受累更重。前索综合征会让损伤以下全部瘫痪，包括双腿；Brown-Séquard 综合征两侧表现不同，通常由刺伤引起；后索综合征丧失轻触觉和位置觉，但力量保留。她虽然能站，但有新的神经体征，仍然需要限制脊柱活动。

slides.title: Spinal shock vs neurogenic shock
slides.body:
Spinal shockNeurogenic shock
ProblemNerves: cord "switched off"Circulation: sympathetic tone lost
You seeFlaccid paralysis, no reflexes, loose sphinctersLow BP, normal or slow pulse
SkinSensation lost below the injuryWarm, dry, flushed below the injury
LastsHours to weeksTemporary

Same word, two problems. Only neurogenic shock drops the blood pressure.
slides.say: These two terms confuse everyone. Spinal shock is a nerve problem. Within about thirty minutes, the cord swells and switches off below the injury: floppy, or flaccid, paralysis, no reflexes, and loss of bladder and bowel control, lasting hours to weeks. Neurogenic shock is a circulation problem. The sympathetic nerves that keep the vessels tight are cut, so the vessels open wide, blood pools, and the pressure falls. Nothing pushes the heart rate up, and the vagus nerve still works, so the pulse is normal or slow, and the skin below the injury is warm, dry and flushed. Only neurogenic shock drops the blood pressure.
slides.sayZh: 这两个词人人都会搞混。脊髓休克是神经问题：大约三十分钟内脊髓肿胀，损伤以下“断电”，出现软瘫（弛缓性瘫痪）、反射消失、大小便失控，可持续数小时到数周。神经源性休克是循环问题：让血管保持收紧的交感神经被切断，血管大幅扩张、血液淤积、血压下降。没有东西推动心率上升，迷走神经又照常工作，所以脉搏正常或偏慢，损伤以下皮肤温暖、干燥、潮红。只有神经源性休克会让血压下降。

slides.title: Neurogenic, bleeding, or both?
slides.body:
NeurogenicHypovolemic
PulseNormal or slowFast
SkinWarm, dry, flushedPale, cool, clammy
CauseVessels too wideVolume lost

Trauma patients can have both. A cut cord can hide the fast pulse of bleeding, and a numb belly won't hurt.
slides.say: On scene, you'll have to decide whether a low blood pressure comes from the spine or from bleeding. In neurogenic shock, the pulse is normal or slow and the skin is warm and dry. In hypovolemic shock, meaning low blood volume, the pulse is fast and the skin is pale, cool and clammy. Here's the PCP-level trap: a trauma patient can have both. With the sympathetic system cut, the heart may not speed up even while the patient bleeds. And with no feeling below the injury, a serious belly injury may cause no pain and no rigid abdomen. So search hard for bleeding before you blame the spine.
slides.sayZh: 在现场，你要判断低血压来自脊柱还是出血。神经源性休克脉搏正常或偏慢、皮肤温暖干燥；低血容量性休克，也就是血容量不足，脉搏快、皮肤苍白湿冷。PCP 层面的陷阱是：创伤病人可能两者兼有。交感神经被切断后，病人即使在出血，心跳也可能不加快。损伤以下没有感觉，腹部即使伤得很重也可能不痛、不发硬。所以先认真找出血，再考虑归咎于脊柱。

slides.title: When to suspect a spinal injury
slides.body:
The book's high-risk list:

  • Significant head injury, multiple trauma, found unresponsive
  • Crash over 60 km/h; unrestrained rollover; ejection
  • Fall over 1 m (over 3 m: much higher risk); diving
  • 30 cm intrusion into the seat; death in the same compartment
  • Penetrating trauma near the spine with a neuro deficit

Penetrating neck wound with a normal neuro exam: no motion restriction needed.
slides.say: When should you suspect a spinal injury? The book says to treat a significant head injury, multiple trauma, or a patient found unresponsive after trauma as a spinal injury. The book also says high-risk mechanisms need full motion restriction whatever your exam shows: for example, a crash over sixty kilometres an hour, an unrestrained rollover, an ejection, a fall from over one metre, with much higher risk over three, a diving injury, thirty centimetres of intrusion into the seat, or a death in the same compartment. One surprise: a penetrating neck wound with a normal neuro exam does not need motion restriction. But in BC, you decide with NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule, as the next slide shows.
slides.sayZh: 什么时候该怀疑脊柱损伤？书里说，严重头部外伤、多发伤、或创伤后被发现无反应的病人，一律按脊柱损伤处理。书里还说，高危机制无论查体结果如何都需要完全的活动限制，例如：车速超过每小时六十公里的碰撞、未系安全带翻车、被甩出车外、从一米以上坠落（超过三米风险显著更高）、跳水受伤、车体侵入座位三十厘米、或同车舱有人死亡。有一点出人意料：颈部穿透伤如果神经检查正常，不需要限制脊柱活动。但在 BC，要用 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则来决定，下一页会讲。

slides.title: Who can skip motion restriction?
slides.body:
The book's reliable patient test:

  • Alert, oriented, no language barrier
  • No brain injury, alcohol or drugs; not too upset
  • No spinal pain or tenderness when you palpate
  • Normal neuro exam; no distracting injury (e.g. femur fracture)

BC: decide with NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule. A normal neuro exam does not rule out a cord injury.
slides.say: Not every trauma patient needs motion restriction. The book describes a reliable patient: alert and oriented, no language barrier, no brain injury, no alcohol or drugs, and not too upset to judge their own pain. If that patient has no pain or tenderness along the spine, a normal neuro exam, and no distracting injury, like a broken femur that hides the neck pain, motion restriction may not be needed. In BC, every licence level decides with NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule. NEXUS checks the same kinds of things; the Canadian rule adds high-risk factors such as age sixty-five or older, a dangerous mechanism, or tingling in the limbs.
slides.sayZh: 并不是每个创伤病人都需要限制脊柱活动。书里描述了“可靠病人”：清醒、定向力好、没有语言障碍、没有脑损伤、没喝酒没用药，情绪也没激动到无法判断自己的疼痛。这样的病人如果沿脊柱没有疼痛或压痛、神经检查正常、也没有牵扯性损伤（比如掩盖颈痛的股骨骨折），就可能不需要限制。在 BC，所有执照级别都用 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则来决定。NEXUS 查的就是这类内容；加拿大规则还加了高危因素，比如六十五岁及以上、危险受伤机制、或四肢刺痛麻木。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: Spinal Management
slides.body:
BC Spinal Management: one protocol for every licence level

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Decide with NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine
  • Manually stabilize head and neck
  • Hard collar
  • Spinal device + foam blocks
  • Secure the body; do not tape the head

PCP adds (from other BC rules)

  • No extra spinal steps: same protocol
  • Functional enquiry in your history (PCP only)
  • Hypovolemia: IV en route, 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; consider TXA for blood loss
  • Head injury: TBI targets (next lesson)
slides.say: Here's BC's Spinal Management protocol, and notice: it has no PCP column. Every licence level decides with NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule, stabilizes the head and neck by hand, applies a hard collar, places the patient on a spinal device with foam blocks, and secures the body, without taping the head. So what does the PCP add? Depth, and tools from other protocols. Your history includes the functional enquiry, a systems review only PCPs do. If the patient is also bleeding and meets the hypovolemia protocol, you start an IV en route, give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassess every five hundred, and consider TXA, or tranexamic acid.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的脊柱管理流程，注意：它没有 PCP 栏。所有执照级别都用 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则决定，徒手稳定头颈，上硬颈托，把病人放上脊柱固定装置并用泡沫头块，固定身体，但不用胶带固定头部。那 PCP 多做什么？深度，以及来自其他流程的工具。你的病史采集包括系统问诊（functional enquiry），这是只有 PCP 才做的系统回顾。如果病人同时在出血、符合低血容量流程，你在转运途中开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，每五百毫升复评，并考虑 TXA，也就是氨甲环酸。

slides.q: A man fell 4 m and can't move his legs. BP 82/50, pulse 54, skin warm and dry below the chest. You're the PCP. What's the best plan?
options: Give atropine for the slow pulse, then transport
Call it neurogenic shock; no need to look for bleeding
Restrict motion, lie flat, oxygen, warmth; IV en route; seek bleeding
Sit him up to 45 degrees to ease his breathing
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A man fell four metres and can't move his legs. His blood pressure is eighty-two over fifty, pulse fifty-four, and the skin is warm and dry below the chest. You're the PCP. What's the best plan? A, give atropine for the slow pulse, then transport. B, call it neurogenic shock, with no need to look for bleeding. C, restrict motion, lie him flat, give oxygen and warmth, start an IV en route, and look for bleeding. D, sit him up to forty-five degrees to ease his breathing. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名男子从四米高处坠落，双腿不能动。血压八十二比五十，脉搏五十四，胸部以下皮肤温暖干燥。你是 PCP，最好的方案是什么？A 先给阿托品纠正慢心率，再转运；B 判定为神经源性休克，不必再找出血；C 脊柱活动限制、平卧、给氧、保暖、出发，途中开静脉，同时继续找出血；D 扶他坐起四十五度，帮助呼吸。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. This looks like neurogenic shock, but a four-metre fall can also cause hidden bleeding, and the cord injury can hide the fast pulse. So use what BC gives you: motion restriction, supine, oxygen, warmth and quick transport, with an IV en route, while you keep searching for blood loss. A is wrong because atropine is outside BC EMR and PCP scope. B ignores hidden bleeding. D moves the spine and can drop the pressure further in vessels that are already wide open.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。这看起来像神经源性休克，但四米坠落同样可能造成隐匿出血，而脊髓损伤会掩盖快心率。所以用 BC 给你的手段：脊柱活动限制、平卧、给氧、保暖、快速转运，途中开静脉，同时继续寻找失血。A 错，阿托品不在 BC 的 EMR 和 PCP 范围内；B 忽略了隐匿出血；D 会移动脊柱，而且在血管已大幅扩张时会让血压更低。

slides.title: Airway and breathing after cord injury
slides.body:
• Open with a jaw thrust, head neutral
  • C3–C5 or higher: diaphragm may stop → ventilate
  • Lower neck to T2: belly breathing, weak cough
  • Watch for paradoxical movement and a rising level
  • Vomiting: log roll as a unit, then suction

Book: assist at 10–12 breaths/min with 12–15 L/min oxygen.
slides.say: With a spinal injury, breathing can fail in ways you might not expect. Open the airway with a jaw thrust and the head neutral, as you already do. Then think about levels. An injury at C3 to C5 or above can paralyse the diaphragm, so the patient may need full ventilation. A lower neck injury spares the diaphragm but knocks out the rib muscles: belly breathing and a weak cough. Watch for paradoxical movement and shallow breaths, and remember that swelling can make the level rise. The book suggests assisting at ten to twelve breaths a minute with twelve to fifteen litres of oxygen. If they vomit, log roll and suction.
slides.sayZh: 脊柱损伤时，呼吸可能以你意想不到的方式出问题。像以前一样，用托颌法开放气道、保持头部中立位。然后从节段去想：C3 到 C5 或更高的损伤可能让膈肌瘫痪，病人可能需要完全的人工通气；颈下段损伤保住了膈肌，却让肋间肌失灵：腹式呼吸、咳嗽无力。注意反常呼吸和浅呼吸，并记住肿胀会让损伤平面上升。书里建议以每分钟十到十二次辅助通气，氧流量每分钟十二到十五升。病人呕吐时，轴线翻身再吸引。

slides.title: Your baseline neuro exam
slides.body:
Ask the patient to…Tests
Bend / straighten the elbowC5 / C7
Move the wristC6
Grip / spread the fingersC8 / T1
Bend and straighten the kneeL3–L4
Toes up / push the foot downL5 / S1–S2

Motor top down, sensation feet up, both sides. Repeat it: the trend matters most.
slides.say: As a PCP, your neuro exam becomes a baseline the hospital compares against, and it can guide decisions about surgery. Test motor function from the top down, on both sides. Bending the elbow tests C5, the wrist C6, straightening the elbow C7, gripping C8, and spreading the fingers T1. In the legs, bending and straightening the knee tests L3 and L4, toes up tests L5, and pushing the foot down tests S1 and S2. Test sensation from the feet up to find the lowest normal level. If the limbs are paralysed, score the GCS motor response with blinking or facial movement. Then repeat: the direction of change matters most.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你的神经检查会成为医院对比用的基线，还能帮助决定是否手术。运动功能从上往下、两侧都查：屈肘查 C5，手腕查 C6，伸肘查 C7，握拳查 C8，张开手指查 T1。下肢：屈伸膝查 L3 和 L4，脚趾上翘查 L5，脚往下踩查 S1 和 S2。感觉从脚往上查，找到最低的正常平面。四肢瘫痪时，GCS 运动评分改用眨眼或面部动作。然后反复检查：变化的方向最重要。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A slow pulse can hide bleeding: keep searching
  • No feeling below the injury: belly exam is unreliable
  • A rising level: breathing may fail next
  • They lose heat fast: keep them warm
  • Atropine: not in BC scope; vasopressors: not on BC list
  • Steroids for cord injury: no longer recommended
slides.say: Now the things that never mattered much as an EMR. First, a slow or normal pulse in trauma doesn't rule out bleeding; the cord injury can block the fast pulse you rely on. Second, a patient who can't feel below the injury may have a quiet abdomen that tells you nothing. Third, if weakness or numbness moves upward, the breathing muscles may be next. Fourth, these patients cool quickly, and cold makes bleeding worse. Fifth, the book uses atropine and vasopressors like dopamine and norepinephrine for neurogenic shock; atropine is outside BC EMR and PCP scope, and those vasopressors aren't on BC's drug list. And steroids are no longer recommended.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲当 EMR 时不太需要操心的事。第一，创伤病人脉搏慢或正常不能排除出血；脊髓损伤会挡住你依赖的快心率。第二，损伤以下没有感觉，肚子安安静静也说明不了什么。第三，如果无力或麻木往上走，下一个可能就是呼吸肌。第四，这些病人很快变冷，而寒冷会加重出血。第五，书里用阿托品，以及多巴胺、去甲肾上腺素这类血管加压药治疗神经源性休克；阿托品不在 BC 的 EMR 和 PCP 范围内，这些血管加压药也不在 BC 考纲药物清单上。另外，已不再推荐用类固醇。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Key levels: C3–C5 breathing; T6 and above, neurogenic shock
  2. Neurogenic shock: low BP, slow pulse, warm dry skin; still hunt for bleeding
  3. Same BC protocol for all; your PCP edge is deeper assessment and shock care

Next: spinal motion restriction, head-injury targets, complications
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: C3 to C5 keeps the diaphragm working, and an injury at T6 or above can cause neurogenic shock. Two: neurogenic shock means low blood pressure, a normal or slow pulse, and warm, dry skin, but in trauma keep looking for bleeding, because the cord injury can hide the usual signs. Three: BC's Spinal Management protocol is the same for every licence level; your edge as a PCP is deeper assessment, a repeated neuro baseline, the functional enquiry, and shock care with an IV en route. Next lesson: motion restriction techniques, head-injury targets, and complications. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，C3 到 C5 维持膈肌工作，T6 及以上的损伤可能引起神经源性休克。二，神经源性休克是低血压、脉搏正常或偏慢、皮肤温暖干燥；但在创伤中要继续找出血，因为脊髓损伤会掩盖常见征象。三，BC 的脊柱管理流程对所有执照级别都一样；你作为 PCP 的优势是更深入的评估、反复做的神经基线、系统问诊，以及途中开静脉处理休克。下节课讲：活动限制技术、颅脑外伤目标值和并发症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
